messages:
tomas: Heads up - ran into a weird parity issue when upgrading a customer POC to python-sdk v0.10.0. The async rerank helper returns nested per-query arrays in one codepath and itemized dicts in another. breaks our search-demo app.

liz: ouch. can you show the tiny repro and the two shapes? sync vs async? helper vs low-level?

tomas: minimal async repro below (using the sample app's batcher):

```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="xxx")
queries = [["find docs about X"], ["find docs about Y"]]
resp = await client.embeddings.rerank_batch(queries)
print(type(resp), resp[:2])
```

Observed SDK output (async, rerank_batch):
`{'vectors': [[...], [...]], 'scores': [[0.92, 0.08], [0.77, 0.23]]}`

But curl-ing the same rerank endpoint returns (raw API):
`[{'embedding': [...], 'score': 0.92}, {'embedding': [...], 'score': 0.08}]`

rachel: that's confusing. our docs (embed+rerank section) show the itemized list, but our python typings for rerank_batch are stubs that return Tuple[List[List[float]], List[List[float]]]. so 3 sources disagree: server, docs, and type hints.

jia: also saw subtle differences between sync and async clients: sync client uses the low-level endpoint and forwards server JSON as-is (list of dicts), async convenience helper tried to be "fast" and returned parallel arrays. that was an intentional historical optimization for numpy stacking. i guess the two implementations drifted.

tomas: exactly. search-demo's batcher expects list-of-items so when it sees parallel arrays it does index lookups and throws IndexError. unhappy POC.

liz: actionable plan: pick a canonical external shape (prefer itemized list-of-objects for clarity), have both clients normalize to that shape in the client layer, and add a tiny conversion util for teams that need parallel arrays for performance. keep parallel-arrays behind an explicit opt-in flag to preserve backcompat.

rachel: agreed on itemized shape. it's easier for partial decodes and for optional fields (score may be missing). i volunteer to update the docs and the sample app in the repo.

jia: i'll draft a PR that: (1) unifies sync+async to return List[EmbeddingResult] objects, (2) adds `redwood.utils.rerank_helpers.to_parallel(resp)` and `from_parallel(...)` helpers, (3) updates typing stubs and overloads, (4) adds unit tests mocking network responses for both shapes and for retry sequences.

tomas: can we add an integration test that simulates an auth retry? previously we've seen a 401->retry path that returned an older formatted body and caused silent corruption. if test covers retry path, we won't regress.

jia: good point. i'll add integration tests that stub a 401 then 200 with different body shapes. that will be part of the PR.

sdk-bot: opened issue #1299: "python-sdk: unify embeddings+rerank response shape; provide conversion helpers; add retry integration tests" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1299

liz: timeline? this is blocking a mid-market POC. patch release would be ideal. can we do a small fix first that normalizes only the async helper (fastest to ship) and follow with the typing/docs fix in the next patch?

jia: yes we can ship a hotfix that normalizes async helper to itemized output and add the helper for parallel arrays. follow-up PR will clean typings/docs and add deprecation note in CHANGELOG.

tomas: thanks! i'll coordinate with the solutions engineer on the POC to try the hotfix once the PR lands. :pray:
